m: This is the ritual direction for the last narrative. The seer is Rudra, the deity Shri Mahasarasvati, the metre anushtubh, the power Bhima, the seed Bhramari, the element the sun, and the form the Samaveda. It is recited to please Shri Mahasarasvati. The meditation begins: she holds in her lotus hands a bell, a spear, a plough, a conch, a pestle, a discus, a bow, and an arrow, her splendour like the cool-rayed moon shining at the edge of a cloud, arisen from Gauri's body, the support of the three worlds, the great ancient one.
Here I worship Sarasvati, crusher of the daityas beginning with Shumbha. Om Klim. The seer said:
Of old, the three worlds and the shares of the sacrifice were taken from the lord of Shachi by the two asuras Shumbha and Nishumbha, relying on the strength of their pride.
Those two likewise took the status of the sun, and likewise the office of the moon, and then Kubera's, Yama's, and Varuna's.
Those two also took the prosperity of the wind and the work of fire. Then the gods were shaken off, their kingdoms lost, defeated.
All the gods, their offices taken, were cast out by those two great asuras. They remembered that unconquered Goddess.
By her a boon was given to us: when remembered in calamities, I will destroy your supreme calamities at that very moment.
Having resolved thus, the gods went to Himavat, lord of mountains. There they then praised the Goddess, the illusion of Vishnu.
The gods said:
Salutation to the Goddess, to the great Goddess, to Shiva, salutation always. Salutation to nature, to the gracious one. Restrained, we have bowed to her.
Salutation to the fierce one, to the eternal, to Gauri, to the supporter, salutation and salutation. To the moonlight, and to her whose form is the moon, to happiness, salutation always.

To the auspicious one we make salutation and salutation, we who have bowed, for increase and for success. To the southwestern one, to the Lakshmi of kings, to Sharvani, salutation and salutation to you.
To Durga, to her who carries one across difficulty, to the essence, to the doer of all, to fame, and likewise to Krishna, to the dark one, salutation always.

To her who is exceedingly gentle and exceedingly fierce, we who have bowed make salutation and salutation. Salutation to the support of the world, to the Goddess, to action, salutation and salutation.

To the Goddess who in all beings is called Vishnu-maya — salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation and salutation. To the Goddess who in all beings is named consciousness — the same salutation. To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of understanding. In the form of sleep. In the form of hunger. In the form of shadow. In the form of power. In the form of craving. In the form of forbearance. In the form of birth. In the form of modesty. In the form of peace. In the form of faith. In the form of beauty. In the form of Lakshmi. In the form of livelihood. In the form of memory. In the form of compassion. In the form of contentment. In the form of the mother. In the form of confusion — salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation and salutation. To her who presides over the senses and over beings in all of them, to the Goddess as the pervasion that is constant in beings, salutation and salutation.

To her who abides pervading this entire world in the form of consciousness — salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation and salutation. Praised of old by the gods because they depended on what they desired, and served through the days by the lord of the gods, may that sovereign, cause of the auspicious, make auspicious and fortunate things for us, and strike down calamities.
She who is now bowed to by us and by the gods, tormented by arrogant daityas, and she who, when remembered, at that very moment destroys all our calamities when our bodies are bent in devotion.
The seer said:
While the gods were engaged in praise in this way, Parvati came there to bathe in the water of the Ganga, O joy of kings.
She, of beautiful brows, said to those gods, Whom are you praising here? And from the sheath of her body, Shiva, who had come forth, said:
This hymn is being made to me by the gods who were cast out by the daitya Shumbha, and who were defeated in battle by Nishumbha, gathered together.
When Ambika had come forth from the sheath of that Parvati's body, she was then sung of in all the worlds as Kaushiki.
And when she had gone forth, Parvati herself became dark. She is called Kalika, and she made her dwelling on the snow mountain.
Then Chanda and Munda, servants of Shumbha and Nishumbha, saw Ambika bearing a supreme form, very beautiful.
They told Shumbha of her, who was exceedingly beautiful: Some woman dwells there, great king, illuminating the snow mountain.
Such a form, an excellent one, has never been seen by anyone anywhere. Let it be known who this Goddess is, and let her be taken, lord of the asuras.
A jewel among women, of exceedingly lovely limbs, lighting the directions with her lustre, she stands there, lord of the daityas. You ought to see her.
Whatever jewels, gems, elephants, horses, and the rest there are, lord, all of them in the three worlds now shine in your house.
Airavata, the jewel of elephants, has been brought from Purandara, and this Parijata tree, and likewise the horse Uchchaihshravas.
This chariot yoked with swans stands in your courtyard, brought here, a thing that was a jewel, the wonder that belonged to Brahma.
This great treasure Mahapadma has been brought from the lord of wealth. The ocean gave a garland of unwithering lotuses, rich in filaments.
Your umbrella of Varuna stands in the house, raining gold. And this excellent chariot, which once belonged to Prajapati.
The spear of Death named the giver of departure, O lord, was taken by you. The noose of the king of the waters is in the possession of your brother.
And all the kinds of jewels born of the ocean belong to Nishumbha. Fire also gave you two garments purified by fire.
Thus, lord of the daityas, all the jewels have been gathered for you. Why is this auspicious jewel among women not taken by you?
The seer said:
Hearing this speech of Chanda and Munda, Shumbha then sent the great asura Sugriva as a messenger to the Goddess.
She is to be told this and that, according to my words, when you have gone. And you should quickly do whatever makes her come of her own pleasure.
He went there, to the very beautiful region of the mountain where she dwells, and then addressed the Goddess smoothly, with a sweet voice.
The messenger said:
Goddess, Shumbha, lord of the daityas, is the supreme lord in the three worlds. I am a messenger sent by him. I have come here into your presence.
He whose command is unobstructed among all the classes of gods, who has conquered every enemy among the daityas: hear what he says.
All the three worlds are mine. The gods are subject to my will. I enjoy all the shares of the sacrifice, each one separately.
The best jewels in the three worlds are under my power, all of them. And likewise the jewel of elephants, the mount of the lord of the gods, has been taken.
The jewel of horses arisen from the churning of the ocean of milk, named Uchchaihshravas, was offered to me by the immortals with a bow.
And whatever other beings that are jewels there are among the gods, the gandharvas, and the serpents, those, O beautiful one, shine in me alone.
We consider you, Goddess, a jewel among women in the world. Come to us, since we are the enjoyers of jewels.
Choose me, or my younger brother Nishumbha, of great valour, you of glancing eyes, since you are indeed a jewel.
You will obtain supreme, unequalled sovereignty by being taken by me. Reflecting with this understanding, come into my possession.
The seer said:
Addressed in this way, the Goddess then spoke, with a deep smile within, Durga, the blessed, the gracious, by whom this world is upheld.
The Goddess said:
What you have said is true. Nothing false has been spoken by you here. Shumbha is lord of the three worlds, and Nishumbha is of that same kind.
But how can what was promised here be done falsely? Hear the promise that was made of old, through little understanding.
He who conquers me in battle, he who casts down my pride, he who is my match in strength in the world, he will be my husband.
So let Shumbha come here, or Nishumbha of great strength. Having conquered me, why delay? Let him take my hand here at once.
The messenger said:
You are arrogant. Do not speak in this way, Goddess, in front of me. What man in the three worlds stands before Shumbha and Nishumbha?
All the gods do not stand face to face in battle even with the other daityas, Goddess. How then you, a woman, alone?
All the gods, beginning with Indra, stood where they could not stand in battle against those beginning with Shumbha. How will you, a woman, go to face them?
You, told by me myself, go to the side of Shumbha and Nishumbha. Otherwise you will go with your pride shaken off by being dragged by the hair.
The Goddess said:
So it is. Shumbha is strong, and Nishumbha is of that kind. What can I do? My promise was made of old without reflection.
You, go. All this that I have said, received with respect, report to the lord of the asuras. And let him do what is fitting.
